turns.text: I'm 7 weeks pregnant and I've had some mild cramping on and off today, which everyone says is normal, but I'm frightened. What should I be looking out for?
Why is some cramping normal in early pregnancy? What's actually causing it?
How do I tell normal stretching pains from pain that means something is wrong?
If I rang my midwife, what would she ask me and what would she advise?
What do early-pregnancy units say are the symptoms that need same-day assessment?
A friend said a warm bath and rest settled her cramps. Is that a reasonable thing to try?
Someone else told me to note the timing and the side of any pain. Why does the side matter?
I have no one to watch my toddler, the nearest hospital is an hour away, and I've been sent home every time I've gone in. How do I get taken seriously if I need to be seen?
Which symptoms in early pregnancy mean I must be seen the same day, no matter what?
Could you give me a plan — what's normal, what isn't, who to call and how to get seen fast if I need to?
